- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by overshoot, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
- In mean-reverting regimes (sentiment oscillating near 0.00), model often underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.00) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; apply 1–3 day lag correction if sentiment shifts sharply.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly declining, model often overestimates upward trend; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
